text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. Variable and function names should describe what they do, so others can follow your logic quickly. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When you need to fix a bug or add a feature later, well-organized code saves time and reduces mistakes.
